skill.name: caam
skill.description: CAAM documents account-profile switching for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI. It covers local OAuth token vaults, isolated profiles, rotation, cooldowns, and a TUI dashboard.
skill.summary: Manage local AI CLI account profiles, rotation, and isolated sessions with CAAM.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick detections are false positives because they are documentation, not executable Ruby or JavaScript code. Confirmed risks remain around remote pipe-to-shell installation, sudo installation, OAuth token vaulting, forced file-based auth storage, sensitive home-directory links, shell aliases, and account rotation after rate limits.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the one-line installer with checksum-verified release downloads and manual, inspectable installation steps.

remediation.issue: OAuth bearer tokens are copied into local vault profiles.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid backing up or restoring bearer tokens; prefer provider-supported login flows and OS credential stores.

remediation.issue: Automatic failover rotates accounts after rate limits.
remediation.suggestion: Remove workflows that continue work by switching accounts after provider rate limits, or require explicit policy approval.

remediation.issue: Isolated profiles link real SSH and Git configuration into generated homes.
remediation.suggestion: Do not link ~/.ssh or ~/.gitconfig by default; request explicit consent and use minimal nonsecret configuration.

remediation.issue: Shell aliases replace familiar AI CLI commands with CAAM wrappers.
remediation.suggestion: Make aliases fully optional, clearly labeled, and easy to remove from shell startup files.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth Bearer Token Vaulting
semantic_findings.description: The skill explains that AI CLI OAuth tokens are plain local files and that possession grants access. It then documents backing up and restoring those tokens between profiles.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text directly describes bearer-token files and a vault workflow for copying them. This is intentional credential handling, not a coincidental file reference.

semantic_findings.title: Rate Limit Circumvention Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to switch accounts after rate limits and rerun commands with another profile. This can enable business-logic abuse of provider usage controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The stated purpose and automatic failover steps explicitly connect rate-limit events to selecting another account and re-executing commands.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Alias Interception of AI Tools
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends aliases that replace normal Claude and Codex commands with a CAAM wrapper. This can hide automatic account switching behind familiar command names.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The alias blocks explicitly map common AI CLI names to caam run. The risk is contextual command interception rather than the Markdown syntax itself.

content.user_title: Manage AI CLI Account Switching with CAAM
content.value_statement: Developers with multiple AI CLI subscriptions need controlled ways to track local authentication profiles. CAAM documents commands for profile backup, activation, isolation, rotation, and status checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains CAAM commands for backing up and activating local AI CLI authentication profiles.
Documents supported auth files for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI.
Describes isolated profile workflows for running separate account sessions.
Covers cooldown tracking, profile health scoring, and automatic failover behavior.
Summarizes TUI dashboard controls for profile activation and status review.
limitations: It is documentation for an external CLI and does not include the CAAM source code.
It cannot verify provider terms of service or account-sharing rules.
It relies on local OAuth file paths that may change when AI CLIs update.
It does not protect stored bearer tokens from local filesystem compromise.

use_cases.title: Track Personal AI CLI Profiles
use_cases.description: Switch between locally saved Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini profiles with visible status checks.

use_cases.title: Separate Work and Personal Sessions
use_cases.description: Use isolated profiles to keep different AI CLI sessions and local homes separate.

use_cases.description: Evaluate cooldown, failover, and profile health behavior before adopting CAAM in a team environment.

output_examples.output: The response explains using CAAM status checks, interpreting profile matches, and confirming the selected provider before launching a session.

output_examples.output: The response lists the rotation behavior, security concerns, policy considerations, and safer alternatives such as manual profile selection.

output_examples.input: A consultant wants separate work and personal Codex sessions.
output_examples.output: The response compares isolated profiles with vault profiles and highlights credential, shell alias, and filesystem boundary risks.

best_practices: Keep CAAM vaults local, encrypted where possible, and excluded from backups or synchronization tools.
Review provider terms and organization policy before using account switching or failover workflows.
Prefer manual profile activation when working with sensitive projects or production credentials.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installation scripts directly into a shell without verification.
Do not use account rotation to continue work after a provider rate limit blocks a session.
Do not expose SSH keys or Git configuration to generated profile homes without explicit consent.

faq.question: What does CAAM manage?
faq.answer: It manages local authentication profile workflows for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI.

faq.question: Does this skill include the CAAM program?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes an external Go CLI and links installation methods for that project.

faq.question: Are OAuth tokens sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that possession of these bearer tokens can grant account access.

faq.question: Can CAAM run profiles in parallel?
faq.answer: The documentation describes isolated profiles that run separate CLI sessions with different local homes.

faq.question: Is automatic failover always appropriate?
faq.answer: No. Users should review provider limits, security policy, and account rules before enabling failover.

faq.question: What is the safest installation approach?
faq.answer: Use verified releases or inspect source and checksums before installing any binary or script.
